title: Investigate unavailable OSM data downloads for completed, archived projects
research_next_step: Use one bounded diagnostic retry of the frozen, scripts-disabled frontend install with the retained cache and informative fetch logging. If successful, run the existing AOI test with synthetic configuration and a socket/DNS guard, then reproduce the original download component. If fetching fails again, capture the endpoint/error and move to independent queue work.
problem: Issue #7227 reports that a completed project cannot supply its building GeoJSON to data requestors. A HOT member identifies archived status as the reason downloads are not updated and suggests considering on-demand refresh for authorized project users.
humanitarian_relevance: Enabling access to validated mapping outputs has a direct operational pathway to requestors using maps. The affected user describes an immediate sharing problem; reach and realized benefit remain unmeasured.

evidence.claim: The reporter could not share completed project map data through the download feature; a later comment explains why post-completion access matters.
A GitHub MEMBER attributes stale downloads to archived project status and proposes considering authorized on-demand fetching. This is historical context, not approval of Humanifest work.

Read-only issue/timeline inspection on 2026-09-08 found OPEN, unassigned, last updated 2026-04-28, and no returned cross-referenced PR. The bounded timeline is not an exhaustive competing-work search.

Four controlled probes of the original hash-checked download handler confirmed a 404 URL opens before status checking and a null browser handle on HTTP 200 shows the same error popup. This is function-level reproduction only; no real browser or deployed service tested.

The pinned get_active_projects service filters recent task/chat activity to PUBLISHED projects, excluding ARCHIVED. This is a source observation, not confirmation of production deployment or the specific missing artifact cause.

GitHub returned the exact prepared scope question authored by humanifest-bot at 2026-09-09T01:38:11Z. Before posting, the issue remained open/unassigned and develop still matched the audited source SHA. This proves delivery, not maintainer approval.

Completed required contribution-policy and frontend setup review, including CI/Docker, CRACO/MSW and exact locked Git manifests. A local network guard rejected four socket/DNS/listen attempts. The single frozen scripts-disabled install timed out after 1,200 seconds during fetching; no target tests ran and environment readiness remains unconfirmed.

code_surface: Inspected pinned DownloadOsmData handler, messages, AOI-only downloadButtons tests, ProjectService.get_active_projects and TM-Extractor v1.0.1. A hash-checked standalone probe exercises the original handler with mocked browser/network objects; no React component coverage located for this handler.
proposed_change: Await scope confirmation for a small frontend failure-handling contribution: check unsuccessful HEAD before navigation, handle a null browser handle, and give guidance based on known facts. It does not restore archived artifacts or close #7227 by itself. Scheduling and permission changes remain separate protected work.
tests: Ran research/fixtures/hot-download-reproduction.mjs against the hash-checked pinned handler on Node v22.16.0: 200 success control, 404 opening before status check, null browser handle misreported as extraction unavailable, and rejected HEAD control all verified; loading cleared in each. No React, browser, target suite or production reproduction. Component plan includes these cases and unsuccessful metadata HEAD requests.

Required contribution docs, manifests, locked Git dependencies, CI/Docker and test setup were inspected.
